```{R}
outliers <- function(x) {
  q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
  upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
  return(x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound)
}

# Apply outlier detection to each variable
outlier_summary <- sapply(prostate, function(x) sum(outliers(x), na.rm = TRUE))

# Print outlier summary (number of outliers)
print(outlier_summary)
```

```{R}
model<-lm(Y ~ X, data = CDI_data)
Estimate_b0<-coef(summary(model))[1, "Estimate"]
Estimate_b1<-coef(summary(model))[2, "Estimate"]

StandardErr_b0<-coef(summary(model))[1, "Std. Error"]
StandardErr_b1<-coef(summary(model))[2, "Std. Error"]

print(paste("Estimate b0: ",Estimate_b0))
print(paste("Estimate b1: ",Estimate_b1))

print(paste("Standard error b0: ",StandardErr_b0))

# Print the equation (refer to lines above)

```


```{R}
#Step 1: H0: intercept =0, HA: intercept is not 0
#        H0: slope=0     , HA: slope is not 0
#Step 2: for testing individual coefficients on a sample one may use a #two sides t statistical test.
#Step 3: the critical t -value applicable given alpha=0.05 and n-2 #degrees of freedom.
#Step 4: decision rule, when t > t critical reject null
#Step 5: calculate t statistic
#First define the significance level — the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true (alpha is the Type I error). That is the % error you are willing to accept.
alpha = 0.05
# Second, to calculate the confidence level, you divide by 2 because it is a two tail test
half_alpha = alpha / 2
# Third: Calculate the degrees of freedom is n - p, that is the number of parameters
df<-nrow(CDI_data) - nrow(summary(model)$coefficients)
# Fourth : Determine the critical t value using the df and the significance levels
value<-formatC(qt(half_alpha,df,lower.tail=FALSE))    
print(paste("Critical T values: ",value))
#coefficients
matrix_coef <- round(summary(model)$coefficients,5)  # Extract coefficients in matrix
matrix_coef   

my_estimates <- round(matrix_coef[ , 1],5)  # Matrix manipulation to extract estimates
#Step 6: For the Intercept, p-value is 0.12917, Pr(>|t|) > 0.05 there no sufficient statistical evidence to reject Ho. For the slope, Pr(>|t|) < 0.05 there is sufficient statistical evidence to reject null. Also t-values (-1.52 and 62.41) confirm, the first is smaller than the 1.965 critical values and the other is larger than t-critical of 1.965
# Get 95% confidence intervals for all coefficients (default)
intervals <- confint(model)
# The confidence interval for the slope (X)
slope_interval <- intervals["X", ]
print(slope_interval)
```

```{R}
set.seed(123)
# Data frame with columns X and Y
prg.hw2 <- function(df, n_sim, sample_size) {
  # Initialize matrix for b0 and b1
  out <- matrix(0, nrow = n_sim, ncol = 2)
  colnames(out) <- c("beta0", "beta1")
  
  for (i in 1:n_sim) {
    # 1. Randomly select row indices
    indices <- sample(1:nrow(df), size = sample_size, replace = FALSE)
    
    # 2. Subset the data
    sample_data <- df[indices, ]
    
    # 3. Fit regression model Y ~ X
    f <- lm(Y ~ X, data = sample_data)
    
    # 4. Record coefficients
    out[i, ] <- f$coefficients
  }
  return(out)
}

# Execute for 1,000 samples of 400 observations
results <- prg.hw2(df = CDI_data, n_sim = 1000, sample_size = 400)
### Calculate the mean and variance of $\beta_0$ and $\beta_1$ based on the 1,000 different regression line and compare against the regression model in question 1 part b.

head(results)

#print for comparison between simulated average values and 1b
print(paste("Estimate b0: ",Estimate_b0))
print(paste("Estimate b1: ",Estimate_b1))

print(paste("Standard error b0: ",StandardErr_b0))
print(paste("Standard error b1: ",StandardErr_b1))

################################## To Compare

average_parameter<-apply(results,2,mean)
print(paste("Avg Estimate b0: ",average_parameter[1]))
print(paste("Avg Estimate b1: ",average_parameter[2]))

average_std<-sqrt(apply(results,2,var))
print(paste("Avg StdardErr b0:",average_std[1]))
print(paste("Avg StdardErr b1:",average_std[2]))

################################## To Compare




```

```{R}
Dataset_1.20 <- read.csv("../Lectures/3/Dataset_1_20.csv", header=FALSE)
f3.4<-lm(Dataset_1.20$V1 ~ Dataset_1.20$V2)
summary(f3.4)
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(f3.4)
ei<-f3.4$residuals
summary(Dataset_1.20$V2)

#We will separate the data based on the median value, we first need to create a data frame with X,Y and errors.

pop1.20<-data.frame(cbind(Dataset_1.20$V1, Dataset_1.20$V2,ei))
p1<-pop1.20[pop1.20[,2]< 5,]
p2<-pop1.20[pop1.20[,2]>=5,]

#get the medians for each sample
M1<-summary(p1[,3])[3]
M2<-summary(p2[,3])[3]
#get the n for each sample
N1<-dim(p1)[1]
N2<-dim(p2)[1]

#calculate dij = abs(error - median.error)
d1<-abs(p1[,3]-M1)
d2<-abs(p2[,3]-M2)

#calculate the pooled variance
s2<-sqrt((var(d1)*(N1-1)+var(d2)*(N2-1))/(N1+N2-2))

#calcualte the t statistics and p value
Den<- s2*sqrt(1/N1+1/N2)
Num<- mean(d1)-mean(d2)

T= Num/Den
1-pt(T,N1+N2-2)
```

```{R}
#loading Prostate Data
load(url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cran/faraway/master/data/prostate.rda"))
head(prostate)


y=prostate$lpsa

#loess Regression

#create a data frame with 2 columns actual and predicted values

#calculate performance statistics
```

```{R}
options("scipen" = 12)
library(dplyr)
#Step 1: Create bands
sd.b1 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, -.5<X, X<1.5)
sd.b2 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, 1.5<X, X<3.5)
sd.b3 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, 3.5<X, X<5.5)
sd.b4 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, 5.5<X, X<7.5)
sd.b5 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, 7.5<X, X<9.5)
#Step 2: Find median X and Y of each band
bands <- data.frame(
  Median.X = c(median(sd.b1$X),median(sd.b2$X),median(sd.b3$X),median(sd.b4$X),median(sd.b5$X)), 
  Median.Y = c(median(sd.b1$Y),median(sd.b2$Y),median(sd.b3$Y),median(sd.b4$Y),median(sd.b5$Y)),
  row.names = c('b1', 'b2','b3', 'b4', 'b5')
)

#Step 3: Plot
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(sales.data) +
    geom_point(aes(x=X, y=Y)) +
    geom_line(data = bands, aes(x=Median.X, y=Median.Y))

#Step 4: Create Neighborhoods
n1 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, -.5<X, X<1.5)
n2 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, 1.5<X, X<3.5)
n3 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, 3.5<X, X<5.5)
n4 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, 5.5<X, X<7.5)
n5 <- dplyr::filter(sales.data, 7.5<X, X<9.5)

#Step 5: Find yhat for each neighborhood
yhat1 <- predict(lm(Y~X,n1), data.frame(X=median(n1$X)))
yhat2 <- predict(lm(Y~X,n2), data.frame(X=median(n2$X)))
yhat3 <- predict(lm(Y~X,n3), data.frame(X=median(n3$X)))
yhat4 <- predict(lm(Y~X,n4), data.frame(X=median(n4$X)))
yhat5 <- predict(lm(Y~X,n5), data.frame(X=median(n5$X)))

#Step 6: Put result in dataframe
neighborhoods <- data.frame(
    Median.X = c(median(n1$X),median(n2$X),median(n3$X),median(n4$X),median(n5$X)), 
    Y.hat = c(yhat1,yhat2,yhat3,yhat4,yhat5),
    row.names = c('n1', 'n2','n3', 'n4', 'n5')
)

#Step 7: Plot with confidence band
ggplot(sales.data) + 
    geom_point(aes(x=X, y=Y)) + 
    geom_line(data = neighborhoods, aes(x=Median.X, y=Y.hat)) +
    geom_smooth(aes(x=X, y=Y), method = 'lm', formula = y~x)





```

```{R}
library(faraway)
library(caret)

#First load data
data(ozone,package="faraway")

# Split the data into training and testing samples
set.seed(1023) 
#split the data into two parts 70-30 split
DataSplit<-createDataPartition(y = ozone$O3, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
#creating the train and test data set
ozone.train<-ozone[DataSplit,]
ozone.test<-ozone[-DataSplit,]
# always check if you have 70% 
num_observations <- nrow(ozone)
num_observations_train <- nrow(ozone.train)
size_test <- (num_observations_train / num_observations)*100
print(paste("Percentage in Train: ",size_test))
# we conclude 71% is sufficiently close



```


```{R}
# Fit linear regression function
attach(ozone)
model <- lm(O3  ~ temp + humidity + ibh, data = ozone.train)
summary(model)
summary(model)
# Obtain,  the  residuals  and  plot  them  against  the fitted values. Also prepare a normal probability plot.
oldpar <- par(mfrow = c(2,2))
plot(model, which = 1:2)
par(oldpar)

```


```{R}
library(car)
car::qqPlot(model, main = "QQ Plot")
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(model)

# Prepare a scatter plot of the data
summary(model)
```


```{R}
library(caret)
PredictedTrain<-predict(model,ozone.train)
ModelTrain<-data.frame(obs = ozone.train$O3, pred=PredictedTrain)
Model_Train=defaultSummary(ModelTrain)

PredictedTest<-predict(model,ozone.test)
ModelTest<-data.frame(obs = ozone.test$O3, pred=PredictedTest)
Model_Test=defaultSummary(ModelTest)

g = rbind(Model_Train,Model_Test)
g
```


```{R}
#We reject the null hypothesis as p.value is 0.00005463 < 0.05 - so, we conclude that the error variances are not constant.
library(lmtest)
bptest(model, studentize = FALSE)

```


```{R}
library(MASS)
# To see more clearly the best value of lambda, we use an ample range
bc=boxcox(model,lambda = seq(-2,2,0.1))
# Narrowing our search
bc=boxcox(model,lambda = seq(-0.5,0.5,0.01))
best.lam=bc$lambda[which(bc$lambda==max(bc$lambda))]
# Obtain the optima lambda
best.lam

model_Transformed<-lm(O3^(best.lam)  ~ temp + humidity + ibh, data = ozone.train)
summary(model_Transformed)

# Seems that model is slightly better in sample

library(caret)
PredictedTrain0<-predict(model_Transformed,ozone.train)
# Reverse back the transformation you took (1/best.lam) so you must reverse
PredictedTrain<-PredictedTrain0^(1/best.lam)
# Now you have apples to apples
ModelTrain<-data.frame(obs = ozone.train$O3, pred=PredictedTrain)
Model_Train=defaultSummary(ModelTrain)
## And on the test data
PredictedTest0<-predict(model_Transformed,ozone.test)
PredictedTest<-PredictedTest0^(1/best.lam)
# Now you have apples to apples
ModelTest<-data.frame(obs = ozone.test$O3, pred=PredictedTest)
Model_Test=defaultSummary(ModelTest)

g = rbind(Model_Train,Model_Test)
g

```

```{R}
library(lmtest)
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(model, which=1)
## Confirm using bptest() R function:
bptest(model, studentize = FALSE)# We have a relatively large number of observations n>100, so we selected FALSE option which assumes normality, in case you have smaller than that use TRUE here.
```


```{R}
library(olsrr)

ols_plot_resid_lev(model)
# Calculate Cook's distance
cooks_dist <- cooks.distance(model)

# Identify observations identified in the OLS PLOT RESID LEV graph
large_leverage_points <- which(cooks_dist > 3 / n)  # You can adjust the threshold (e.g., 3/n) to match the outlier and leverage diagnosis graph results

# Print the indices of observations above the desired threshold on the Cook's distance
print(large_leverage_points)
```


```{R}
plot(model,which=3)

# Identify observations identified in the OLS PLOT RESID LEV graph as outliers
outlier_points <- which(cooks_dist > 3 / n)  # You can adjust the threshold (e.g., 3/n) to match the outlier count in the leverage diagnosis graph

# Print the indices of observations above the desired threshold on the Cook's distance
print(outlier_points)

```


```{R}
# Use a visual

library(car)
influencePlot(model, id="noteworthy", main="Influence Plot",
              sub="Circle size is proportional to Cook's distance")
#Compute Bonferroni Critical Value is 4.199773
p=3
Bonferroni_Critical_Value<-abs(qt(.05/(n*p),n-p-1))

#are there of them bad outliers? 
outlier_test <- outlierTest(model)

knitr::kable(cbind(abs(outlier_test$rstudent),"<",Bonferroni_Critical_Value), align = "c",
caption = "Largest Outlier vs. Bonferroni Critical Value")

#Since Abs(-3.124428) is lower than 3.832128, we conclude that point West Virginia or Utah (2.52) are influential outliers, please note that Bonferroni applies an extra conservative approach.
outlier_test
```

```{R}
# ---- 1(e) Brown–Forsythe test exactly per spec ----
library(car)

# Residuals and fitted from the Problem 1 model
r     <- residuals(f1)
fhat  <- fitted(f1)

# Group by the 40 smallest fitted values (group A) vs the rest (group B)
ord <- order(fhat)
grp <- rep("B_rest", length(fhat))
grp[ord[1:40]] <- "A_small40"
grp <- factor(grp, levels = c("A_small40", "B_rest"))

# Brown–Forsythe test (Levene with center = "median") on residuals by group
bf <- leveneTest(r ~ grp, center = "median")
print(bf)
```

```{R}
cv5_linear_caret <- function(
  data,
  response,            # character: name of response variable (numeric)
  predictor,           # character: name of predictor variable
  seed = 1023,         # fixed seed for reproducibility
  fit_fun = NULL,      # optional: custom fit function for "selected model in part (a)"
  ...
) {
  # Dependencies
  if (!requireNamespace("caret", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Package 'caret' is required. Please install it: install.packages('caret')")
  }
  
  # Basic checks
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(data))
  if (!all(c(response, predictor) %in% names(data))) {
    stop("response/predictor must be columns in 'data'.")
  }
  if (!is.numeric(data[[response]])) {
    stop("The response variable must be numeric for caret::defaultSummary (regression).")
  }
  if (nrow(data) != 440) {
    warning(sprintf("Data has %d rows; proceeding anyway but function was designed for 440.", nrow(data)))
  }
  
  # Build the model formula
  form <- as.formula(paste(response, "~", predictor))
  
  # Model is linear regression (lm)
  if (is.null(fit_fun)) {
    fit_fun <- function(formula, dat, ...) stats::lm(formula, data = dat, ...)
  }
  
  # Create 5 equal folds of 88 each using a fixed seed
  set.seed(seed)
  n <- nrow(data)
  k <- 5
  if (n %% k != 0) stop("nrow(data) must be divisible by 5 to guarantee equal fold sizes.")
  
  # Random permutation + exact equal fold assignment
  idx <- sample(n)                         # random permutation
  fold_id <- rep(1:k, each = n / k)        # 1..5, exactly 88 each for n=440
  fold_id <- fold_id[order(idx)]           # map to original row order
  folds <- split(seq_len(n), fold_id)      # list of test indices per fold
  
  # Storage for metrics
  train_metrics <- vector("list", k)
  test_metrics  <- vector("list", k)
  models        <- vector("list", k)
  
  # Cross-validation loop
  for (i in seq_len(k)) {
    test_idx  <- folds[[i]]
    train_idx <- setdiff(seq_len(n), test_idx)
    
    data.train <- data[train_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    data.test  <- data[test_idx,  , drop = FALSE]
    
    # Fit your selected model from part (a); default: lm
    model <- fit_fun(form, data.train, ...)
    models[[i]] <- model
    
    # ---- Training metrics (caret::defaultSummary) ----
    PredictedTrain <- predict(model, newdata = data.train)
    ModelTrain <- data.frame(
      obs  = data.train[[response]],
      pred = PredictedTrain
    )
    Model_Train <- caret::defaultSummary(ModelTrain)  # RMSE, Rsquared, MAE
    train_metrics[[i]] <- as.data.frame(as.list(Model_Train))
    train_metrics[[i]]$Fold <- i
    
    # ---- Testing metrics (caret::defaultSummary) ----
    PredictedTest <- predict(model, newdata = data.test)
    ModelTest <- data.frame(
      obs  = data.test[[response]],
      pred = PredictedTest
    )
    Model_Test <- caret::defaultSummary(ModelTest)    # RMSE, Rsquared, MAE
    test_metrics[[i]] <- as.data.frame(as.list(Model_Test))
    test_metrics[[i]]$Fold <- i
  }
  
  # Bind per-fold metrics
  train_df <- do.call(rbind, train_metrics)[, c("Fold", "RMSE", "Rsquared", "MAE")]
  test_df  <- do.call(rbind,  test_metrics)[,  c("Fold", "RMSE", "Rsquared", "MAE")]
  
  # Summaries: mean and sd across folds
  summarize_metrics <- function(df) {
    data.frame(
      Metric = c("RMSE", "Rsquared", "MAE"),
      Mean   = c(mean(df$RMSE), mean(df$Rsquared), mean(df$MAE)),
      SD     = c(sd(df$RMSE),   sd(df$Rsquared),   sd(df$MAE))
    )
  }
  summary_train <- summarize_metrics(train_df)
  summary_test  <- summarize_metrics(test_df)
  
  # Return a structured result
  list(
    call = match.call(),
    formula = form,
    seed = seed,
    fold_sizes = sapply(folds, length),
    folds = folds,                       # test indices per fold
    per_fold_train = train_df,           # RMSE/R2/MAE by fold (train)
    per_fold_test  = test_df,            # RMSE/R2/MAE by fold (test)
    summary_train = summary_train,       # Means and SDs (train)
    summary_test  = summary_test,        # Means and SDs (test)
    models = models                      
  )
}

```


```{R}
set.seed(1023)  
cv_out <- cv5_linear_caret(
  data = data2,
  response = "Y",
  predictor = c("X2","X5","X7","X8","X11","X12","X13.1","X13.2","X13.3")
)
# Inspect fold sizes (should be all 88)
cv_out$fold_sizes
# Per-fold metrics (training and testing)
cv_out$per_fold_train
cv_out$per_fold_test
# Summaries across folds
cv_out$summary_train
cv_out$summary_test

```

```{R}
require(stats); require(graphics) 
longley_data<-data.frame(longley)

# Linear with all predictors
longley.reg <- stats::lm(Employed ~ .,data=longley_data)
summary(longley.reg)
summary(longley.reg)
# Coefficients
coeff.lm.df <- data.frame(Linear = longley.reg$coefficients)
coeff.lm.df$Coefficients <- rownames(coeff.lm.df)
rownames(coeff.lm.df) <- NULL
coeff.lm.df <- dplyr::select(coeff.lm.df, Coefficients, Linear) 
coeff.q1.df <-
  coeff.lm.df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Linear = ifelse(Linear == 0, "--", scales::comma(Linear, accuracy = 1e-4)))
knitr::kable(coeff.q1.df, caption = "Model Coefficients")
```


```{R}
set.seed(1023)
longley.reg.both <- olsrr::ols_step_both_p(longley.reg, pent=0.35, prem=0.05, details=TRUE)

plot(longley.reg.both)
longley.reg.sw.final <- longley.reg.both$model
summary(longley.reg.sw.final)
summary(longley.reg.sw.final)
# Coefficients
coeff.sw.df <- data.frame(Stepwise = longley.reg.sw.final$coefficients)
coeff.sw.df$Coefficients <- rownames(coeff.sw.df)
coeff.q1.df <-
  coeff.q1.df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(coeff.sw.df, by = "Coefficients") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Stepwise = ifelse(dplyr::coalesce(Stepwise, 0) == 0, "--", 
                                  scales::comma(Stepwise, accuracy = 1e-4)))
knitr::kable(coeff.q1.df, caption = "Model Coefficients")
```


```{R}
set.seed(1023)
olsrr::ols_vif_tol(longley.reg)
longley.cor.df <- data.frame(stats::cor(longley_data))
longley.cor.df$Predictor1 <- colnames(longley.cor.df)
longley.cor.df <-
  longley.cor.df %>%
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = c('Predictor1'), variable.name = 'Predictor2', value.name = 'Correlation') %>%
  dplyr::filter(Correlation >= 0.8 & Predictor1 != Predictor2) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Correlation)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number() == 1 | dplyr::lag(Correlation, 1) != Correlation)
knitr::kable(longley.cor.df, caption = "Highly Correlated Predictors")

# Separate x and y
x <- data.matrix(dplyr::select(longley, -Employed))
y <- longley$Employed

# Cross Validate and calculate best lambda
longley.ridge.cv <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(x, y, alpha=0, nlambda=100,lambda.min.ratio=0.0001)
best.lambda.ridge <- longley.ridge.cv$lambda.min
plot(longley.ridge.cv)

print(paste0("Ridge best lambda of ", round(best.lambda.ridge, digits = 3)))

# Coefficients Best Lambda
coeff.ridge.df <- stats::coef(longley.ridge.cv , s = best.lambda.ridge)
coeff.ridge.df <- data.frame(Coefficients = coeff.ridge.df@Dimnames[[1]],
                             Ridge = coeff.ridge.df@x)
coeff.q1.df <-
  coeff.q1.df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(coeff.ridge.df, by = "Coefficients") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Ridge = ifelse(dplyr::coalesce(Ridge, 0) == 0, "--", 
                               scales::comma(Ridge, accuracy = 1e-4)))
knitr::kable(coeff.q1.df, caption = "Model Coefficients")
```


```{R}
set.seed(1023)
# Cross Validate and calculate best lambda
reg.lasso.cv <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(x, y, alpha=1, nlambda=100, lambda.min.ratio=0.0001)
best.lambda.lasso <- reg.lasso.cv$lambda.min
plot(reg.lasso.cv)
print(paste0("Lasso best lambda of ", round(best.lambda.lasso, digits = 3)))

# Coefficients
coeff.lasso <- stats::coef(reg.lasso.cv, s = "lambda.min")
coeff.lasso.names <- coeff.lasso@Dimnames[[1]]
coeff.lasso.df <- data.frame()
for (i in 1:length(coeff.lasso)) {
  df <- data.frame(Coefficients = coeff.lasso.names[i],
                   Lasso = coeff.lasso[i])
  coeff.lasso.df <- rbind(df, coeff.lasso.df)
}
coeff.q1.df <-
  coeff.q1.df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(coeff.lasso.df, by = "Coefficients") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Lasso = ifelse(dplyr::coalesce(Lasso, 0) == 0, "--", 
                               scales::comma(Lasso, accuracy = 1e-4)))
knitr::kable(coeff.q1.df, caption = "Model Coefficients")
rm(df)
```


```{R}
set.seed(1023)

rm(df)
```

```{R}
set.seed(1023)
Employed.predictors <- colnames(dplyr::select(longley, -Employed))
longley_data$Employed.lm <- stats::predict(longley.reg, longley_data)
longley_data$Employed.sw.lm <- stats::predict(longley.reg.sw.final, longley_data)
longley_data$Employed.ridge <-
  stats::predict(longley.ridge.cv, s = best.lambda.ridge, 
                 newx = data.matrix(longley_data[Employed.predictors]))[,1]
longley_data$Employed.lasso <-
  stats::predict(reg.lasso.cv, s = best.lambda.lasso, 
                 newx = data.matrix(longley_data[Employed.predictors]))[,1]
longley_data$Employed.en <-
  stats::predict(reg.enet.cv, s = best.lambda.enet, 
                 newx = data.matrix(longley_data[Employed.predictors]))[,1]
longley_data$Employed.huber <- stats::predict(longley.reg.huber, longley_data)

# SST, SSE, and R2
sst <- sum((longley_data$Employed - mean(longley_data$Employed))^2)
sse.lm <- sum((longley_data$Employed - longley_data$Employed.lm)^2)
sse.sw <- sum((longley_data$Employed - longley_data$Employed.sw.lm)^2)
sse.ridge <- sum((longley_data$Employed - longley_data$Employed.ridge)^2)
sse.lasso <- sum((longley_data$Employed - longley_data$Employed.lasso)^2)
sse.enet <- sum((longley_data$Employed - longley_data$Employed.en)^2)
sse.huber <- sum((longley_data$Employed - longley_data$Employed.huber)^2)
data.frame(Model = c('Linear', 'Stepwise', 'Ridge', 'Lasso', 'Elastic Net', 'Huber'),
           R2 = c(round(1 - sse.lm / sst, digits = 4),
                  round(1 - sse.sw / sst, digits = 4),
                  round(1 - sse.ridge / sst, digits = 4),
                  round(1 - sse.lasso / sst, digits = 4),
                  round(1 - sse.enet / sst, digits = 4),
                  round(1 - sse.huber / sst, digits = 4)),
           MSE = c(round(sse.lm / nrow(longley_data), digits = 4),
                  round(sse.sw / nrow(longley_data), digits = 4),
                  round(sse.ridge / nrow(longley_data), digits = 4),
                  round(sse.lasso / nrow(longley_data), digits = 4),
                  round(sse.enet / nrow(longley_data), digits = 4),
                  round(sse.huber / nrow(longley_data), digits = 4))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(R2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "R2 of Different Models")
```


```{R}
# Data Preparations

GNPPC<-data.frame(longley_data$GNP/longley$Population)

# New Predictors
Employed.predictors2 <- cbind(GNPPC,longley_data$Unemployed,longley_data$Armed.Forces,longley_data$GNP.deflator,longley_data$Year)
#New Data
longley2<-cbind(longley_data$Employed,Employed.predictors2)
colnames(longley2)<-c("Employed","GNP.Per.Capita","Unemployed","Armed.Forces","GNP.deflator","Year")

# Least Squares using full data
longley.reg.full2 <- stats::lm(Employed ~ ., data = longley2)
summary(longley.reg.full2)
summary(longley.reg.full2)
# Huber's robust method using full data
reg.huber.full2 <- MASS::rlm(Employed ~ ., psi = psi.huber, data = longley2)
summary(reg.huber.full2)
summary(reg.huber.full2)
# Coefficients
coeff.q2.df <- data.frame(Linear = longley.reg.full2$coefficients)
coeff.q2.df$Coefficients <- rownames(coeff.q2.df)
rownames(coeff.q2.df) <- NULL
coeff.q2.huber.df <- data.frame(Huber = reg.huber.full2$coefficients)
coeff.q2.huber.df$Coefficients <- rownames(coeff.q2.huber.df)
coeff.q2.df <-
  coeff.q2.df %>%
  dplyr::select(Coefficients, Linear) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(coeff.q2.huber.df, by = "Coefficients") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Diff = round(abs(Linear - Huber), digits = 4),
                Linear = ifelse(Linear == 0, "--", scales::comma(Linear, accuracy = 1e-4)),
                Huber = ifelse(dplyr::coalesce(Huber, 0) == 0, "--",
                               scales::comma(Huber, accuracy = 1e-4))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Diff))
knitr::kable(coeff.q2.df, caption = "Model Coefficients")

# SST, SSE, and R2
sst.q2 <- sum((longley_data$Employed - mean(longley_data$Employed))^2)
sse.q2.lm <- sum(longley.reg.full2$residuals^2)
sse.q2.huber <- sum(reg.huber.full2$residuals^2)
data.frame(Model = c('Linear', 'Huber.Robust'),
           R2 = c(round(1 - sse.q2.lm / sst.q2, digits = 4),
                  round(1 - sse.q2.huber / sst.q2, digits = 4)),
           MSE = c(round(sse.q2.lm / nrow(fat), digits = 4),
                   round(sse.q2.huber / nrow(fat), digits = 4))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "R2 of Different Models")
```


```{R}
olsrr::ols_plot_resid_lev(longley.reg.full2)
olsrr::ols_plot_cooksd_chart(longley.reg.full2)

# Huber Weights
longley2$weights <- reg.huber.full2[["w"]]

# Lowest Weights
longley2 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Observation = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(weights) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number() <= 5) %>%
  dplyr::select(Observation, Employed, weights) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Observations with 5 Lowest Weights", row.names = FALSE)
```


```{R}
# Deleted Studentized Residual
longley2$del.stud.res <- abs(stats::rstudent(longley.reg.full2))
alpha <- 0.05
n <- nrow(longley2)
p <- length(longley.reg.full2$coefficients)
longley2$t.val <- abs(stats::qt(1-alpha/(2*n), n-p-1))

longley2 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Observation = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(del.stud.res)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(del.stud.res >= t.val) %>%
  dplyr::select(Observation, Employed, del.stud.res, t.val) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Influential Observations", row.names = FALSE)

# Plot
ggplot2::ggplot(longley2, ggplot2::aes(x=Year, y=Unemployed)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() + # Show dots
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    label=rownames(longley2),
    nudge_x = 0.25, nudge_y = 0.25,
    check_overlap = T)
```

### ../Modules/Week 7/Remedial Measures Rcodes/Ridge Lasso and ElasticNet -BodyFat.Rmd

```{R}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


```{R}
library(glmnet)
BodyFat<- read.csv("../Modules/Week 7/Remedial Measures Rcodes/Body Fat.csv")
#need to define X and Y matrix for glmnet
#take out Y and law indicator from data for X (all independent variable)
#to get all the Xs (independent Variables)
x <- model.matrix(Y~., BodyFat)[,-c(1)]
#our dependent variable
y <- BodyFat$Y
RidgeMod <- glmnet(x, y, alpha=0, nlambda=100,lambda.min.ratio=0.0001)

#coefficents for the smallest lambda
coef(RidgeMod, s = min(RidgeMod$lambda))
#coefficents for the largest lambda
coef(RidgeMod, s = max(RidgeMod$lambda))
```


```{R}
CvRidgeMod <- cv.glmnet(x, y, alpha=0, nlambda=100,lambda.min.ratio=0.0001)
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
plot(CvRidgeMod)
#get the optimal lambda
best.lambda.ridge <- CvRidgeMod$lambda.min
best.lambda.ridge 
coef(CvRidgeMod , s = "lambda.min")

```


```{R}
predict(RidgeMod, s=best.lambda.ridge, type="coefficients")[1:4, ]
```


```{R}
LassoMod <- glmnet(x, y, alpha=1, nlambda=100,lambda.min.ratio=0.0001)
#coefficents for the smallest lambda
coef(LassoMod, s = min(LassoMod$lambda))
#coefficents for the largest lambda
coef(LassoMod, s = max(LassoMod$lambda))

plot(LassoMod,xvar="norm",label=TRUE)
CvLassoMod <- cv.glmnet(x, y, alpha=1, nlambda=100,lambda.min.ratio=0.0001)
plot(CvLassoMod)
#get the optimal lambda
best.lambda.lasso <- CvLassoMod$lambda.min
best.lambda.lasso
coef(CvLassoMod, s = "lambda.min")
```


```{R}
EnetMod <- glmnet(x, y, alpha=0.5, nlambda=100,lambda.min.ratio=0.0001)
CvElasticnetMod <- cv.glmnet(x, y,alpha=0.5,nlambda=100,lambda.min.ratio=0.0001)
best.lambda.enet <- CvElasticnetMod$lambda.min
best.lambda.enet
coefficients(EnetMod,s=best.lambda.enet)
coef(CvElasticnetMod, s = "lambda.min")
```


```{R}
f<-lm(Y~.,data=BodyFat)
y_hat.ridge <- predict(RidgeMod, s = best.lambda.ridge, newx = x)
y_hat.lasso <- predict(LassoMod, s = best.lambda.lasso, newx = x)
y_hat.enet <- predict(CvElasticnetMod , s = best.lambda.enet, newx = x)

###(## Model Performance on the Train Data
library(caret)
## Linear Regression Model
Predicted<-f$fitted.values
ModelTrain.reg<-data.frame(obs = BodyFat$Y, pred=Predicted)
reg<-defaultSummary(ModelTrain.reg)

## Ridge Regression Model
Predicted<-c(y_hat.ridge)
ModelTrain.ridge<-data.frame(obs = BodyFat$Y, pred=Predicted)
ridge<-defaultSummary(ModelTrain.ridge)

## Lasso Regression Model
Predicted<-c(y_hat.lasso)
ModelTrain.lasso<-data.frame(obs = BodyFat$Y, pred=Predicted)
lasso<-defaultSummary(ModelTrain.lasso)

## Elastic Net Regression Model
Predicted<-c(y_hat.enet)
ModelTrain.enet<-data.frame(obs = BodyFat$Y, pred=Predicted)
enet<-defaultSummary(ModelTrain.enet)

data.frame(rbind(reg,ridge,lasso,enet))
```

```{R}
library(caret)
#convert defaults from "Yes" and "No" to 1's and 0's

predicted_probabilities <- predict(lmodr1, wcgs, type="response")

#using 0.5 as a cutoff to predict the class
predictions <- ifelse(predicted_probabilities > 0.5, 1, 0)

confusion_matrix
```

```{R}
cutoff.prg<-function(pred,act){
# pred<-predicted_probabilities
# act<-true_labels
p<-seq(0,1,0.01)
n<-length(p)
out<-matrix(0,nrow=n,ncol=12)
for(i in 1:n){
predictions <- ifelse(pred >p[i], 1, 0)
confusion_matrix <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(predictions),as.factor(act),mode="prec_recall", positive = "1")
out[i,]<-cbind(p=p[i],t(confusion_matrix[[4]]))
}
dimnames(out)[[2]]<-c("p","Sensitivity","Specificity","Pos Pred Value","Neg Pred Value","Precision","Recall", "F1","Prevalence","Detection Rate","Detection Prevalence", "Balanced Accuracy")
out
}

test<-cutoff.prg(predicted_probabilities,true_labels)
plot(test[,1],test[,8],xlab="cut off",ylab="F1")
test[which.max(test[,8]),]

```


```{R}
plot(test[,1],                           
     test[,8],
     type = "l",
     col = 2,
     xlab = "cut off",
     ylab = "rates")
 
# Add line graphs of other two data set
lines(test[,1],                             
      test[,2],
      type = "l",
      col = 3)
lines(test[,1],                             
      test[,3],
      type = "l",
      col = 4)
# Add legend in top right corner
legend("topright",                           
       c("F1", "Sensitivity", "Specificity"),
       lty = 1,
       col = 2:4)
```

```{R}
  )
```

```{R}

summary(modn)
anova(modn,test="Chi")
drop1(modn,test="Chi")

pred.dat<-data.frame(cbind(Y=Bikeshare$bikers,Yhat_P=modp$fitted.values,Yhat_NP=modn$fitted.values))
```
